questions.question: A country's balance of trade is:
options: The difference between its exports and its imports — a surplus when exports exceed imports, a deficit when imports win
The total value of everything it produces in a year
The number of trade agreements it has signed
The ratio of export prices to import prices

questions.question: Why does exporting raw ore while importing finished machinery mark a peripheral trade profile?
options: Because ore is heavier than machinery
Because most value is added during processing, so the country sells cheap and buys expensive, and the money drifts one way
Because machinery cannot be produced in the southern hemisphere
Because raw materials never find buyers

questions.question: Angola swinging with oil and Botswana holding its breath with every diamond downturn illustrate:
options: The advantage of specialising in one export
That mineral exporters always run trade surpluses
The risk of commodity dependence — living on a price rollercoaster the country does not steer
That commodity prices are fixed by producers

questions.question: Within South Africa's export basket, the vehicles assembled in Kariega, East London, Durban and Rosslyn matter because:
options: They are the country's only export
They are exempt from all import duties
Vehicle exports never fluctuate in price
They are manufactured, value-added exports — exactly the basket development policy works to enlarge

subtopics.title: Terms of Trade and Trading Relationships

questions.question: A country's terms of trade deteriorate when:
options: Import prices pull ahead of export prices, so ever more export tonnage is needed to afford the same imports
Its exports exceed its imports
Its currency strengthens against the dollar
It signs a new trade agreement

questions.question: Primary product prices tend to slide against manufactured goods prices over the long run because:
options: Raw materials are becoming scarcer everywhere
Raw materials face endless competition and substitution while manufactured goods shelter behind technology, patents and brands
Manufactured goods are heavier to transport
World demand for food is falling

questions.question: Rich-world farm subsidies are the sore point of protectionism because:
options: They raise food prices in Europe and America
They apply only to luxury crops
They let European and American produce undercut African farmers on their own continent
They fund agricultural research

questions.question: The African Continental Free Trade Area is an example of:
options: A fair trade certification scheme
Protectionism against African imports
A bilateral agreement with the United States
A trade bloc — freeing trade among members to stitch Africa's many small markets into one continental market

subtopics.title: Globalisation and Its Impact on Development

questions.question: The main drivers of globalisation are:
options: Radically cheaper transport — above all the shipping container — instant communication, and lowered trade barriers
Rising tariffs and stricter border controls
The decline of manufacturing worldwide
Fixed exchange rates between all currencies

questions.question: A transnational corporation (TNC) is defined by:
options: Selling products in more than one language
Headquarters in one country, factories in others and customers everywhere — like Samsung, Nestlé, Sasol or Shoprite
Being owned by more than one government
Employing more than ten thousand workers

questions.question: The race to the bottom describes:
options: Countries competing to lower shipping costs
Falling commodity prices during a recession
TNCs extracting tax holidays and light regulation from small governments, then relocating the moment cheaper labour appears elsewhere
The decline of the fishing industry

questions.question: The 2008 financial crisis cutting South African exports and jobs within months demonstrates that:
options: South African banks caused the crisis
Exports are unrelated to global conditions
Globalisation protects countries from external events
Interconnection is a transmission line for shocks — crises born elsewhere arrive quickly in open economies

questions.question: South Korea's export-led recipe ran:
options: Cheap-labour textiles first, foreign exchange banked, deliberate reinvestment in schooling and infrastructure, then the climb — textiles to steel to ships to cars to semiconductors
Semiconductors first, then textiles once wealthy
Import substitution behind closed borders throughout
Agriculture only, with no manufacturing stage

questions.question: The South Korean state's role in take-off was to:
options: Stand back and let markets decide everything
Shelter infant industries, steer bank credit, and make support conditional on export success
Nationalise all export industries permanently
Ban foreign investment entirely

questions.question: One structural criticism of export-led development is that:
options: Manufacturing employs too few people
Exports cannot earn foreign exchange
It presumes open, growing world markets — and if every country climbs at once, the markets flood
It requires no investment in education

questions.question: South Africa's honest position on the export-led route is that:
options: The route is closed to South Africa entirely
The Tigers' conditions are easy to replicate here
Export-led growth requires no state capacity
We run export-led elements — vehicles, citrus, AGOA access — while carrying burdens the Tigers never did: distance, power cuts, skills shortages and rigid input costs

questions.question: In the street picture, the spaza end of the world economy stands for:
options: Countries selling raw materials — ore, raw cocoa, unprocessed fruit — cheaply, while buying processed goods dearly
Countries with the largest retail sectors
Countries that refuse to trade internationally
Countries that only import food

questions.question: A kilogram of cocoa beans earning a farmer a few rand while the processed, branded slabs sell for hundreds shows that:
options: Chocolate is overpriced everywhere
The value added settles where the processing happens, never where the pod was picked
Farmers should stop growing cocoa
Transport costs consume the difference

questions.question: South Africa 'works both ends of the street' because:
options: It has both spaza shops and supermarkets
It imports and exports the same products
It sells raw platinum, coal and iron ore spaza-style while its vehicle plants sell finished cars supermarket-style
Its shops are owned by foreign companies

subtopics.title: Swapping Bags of Oranges for Phones

questions.question: One bag of oranges swapping for one phone this year, but the same phone costing four bags next season, illustrates:
options: Deteriorating terms of trade — working and shipping more while affording less, through no fault of the producer
An improvement in the orange grower's terms of trade
A trade surplus for the orange grower
The effect of a drought on phone production

questions.question: The swap rate drifts against raw sellers over time because:
options: Oranges spoil faster than phones
Almost anyone can grow oranges while only a few firms can build phones — and the phone-builders own the patents and brands
Phones are subsidised by governments
Orange farmers refuse to modernise

questions.question: Fair trade certification pushes back against the drifting swap rate by:
options: Banning imports of manufactured goods
Fixing the world price of all commodities
Promising the farmer a guaranteed floor price plus a social premium, so the swap rate cannot collapse under her mid-season
Paying farmers in foreign currency

questions.question: The 'team rule' most worth arguing about in an essay is:
options: The founding of SADC
The abolition of all tariffs worldwide
AGOA's expiry provisions
Rich-world farm subsidies — wealthy countries subsidising their farmers until their produce undercuts African harvests in African markets

questions.question: The correct order of rungs on the Tigers' ladder is:
options: T-shirts, schools and steel, ships, cars, semiconductors
Semiconductors, cars, ships, steel, T-shirts
Cars, T-shirts, semiconductors, ships, steel
Ships, cars, T-shirts, steel, semiconductors

questions.question: The warning that 'the ladder needs buyers waiting at the top' means:
options: Ladders require safety inspections
The strategy worked because rich markets stayed open — and they cannot absorb every country climbing at once
Only wealthy countries may join trade blocs
Export prices always rise over time

questions.question: 'The bottom rungs bruise' refers to:
options: The cost of factory construction
High tariffs on textile exports
The first generation working brutal hours at low pay, with unions suppressed, so the next generation can study engineering — raising the question of who pays for take-off
The difficulty of learning to sew

questions.question: South Africa 'climbing with a heavy backpack' means:
options: The country exports mostly backpacks
The ladder is closed to African countries
South Africa refuses export-led policies
We are on the ladder — vehicle exports prove it — but climb carrying power cuts, distant markets and a skills gap the Tigers did not carry
